'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[2022 Ukrainian summer counteroffensive]]
****Ukrainian [[president of Ukraine|presidential]] advisor [[Oleksiy Arestovych]] says that an [[military operation|operation]] to recapture the [[Kherson Oblast]] has started. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2022/jul/28/russia-ukraine-war-live-news-kyiv-region-hit-by-rocket-attack-governor-says-fight-to-liberate-kherson-has-begun-ukraine-claims (''The Guardian'')]
***[[Battle of Donbas (2022)|Battle of Donbas]]
****Russian forces shell [[Bakhmut]] in [[Donetsk Oblast]] with the [[BM-27 Uragan]] [[Multiple rocket launcher|MLRS]], killing three civilians and injuring three others. Six apartment blocks and six detached houses are also destroyed or damaged. [https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/3539035-russians-strike-bakhmut-with-uragan-mlrs-three-civilians-killed.html (Ukrinform)]
**[[Belarusian involvement in the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Russian Armed Forces|Russian forces]] in [[Belarus]] launch 25 [[ballistic missile]]s into northern Ukraine. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/jul/28/russian-forces-fire-barrage-missiles-northern-ukraine-from-belarus (''The Guardian'')]
**Russia launches [[cruise missile]] strikes from the [[Black Sea]] on the [[Kyiv Oblast]] for the first time in weeks, with missiles striking [[Bucha, Kyiv Oblast|Bucha]], [[Lyutizh]], and [[Vyshhorod]]. At least fifteen people, including five civilians, are injured, according to Kyiv governor [[Oleksiy Kuleba]]. [https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-kyiv-e85d2709f3f6be7eff1b8d278e4d2be9 (AP)] [https://www.axios.com/2022/07/28/russia-strike-kyiv-kherson-counteroffensive (''Axios'')]
**Russian missiles strike [[Kropyvnytskyi]], damaging facilities owned by Kropyvnytskyi Flight Academy and [[Air Urga]]. Five people are killed and 25 others are injured. [https://news.yahoo.com/rocket-shelling-kropyvnytskyi-5-dead-123518473.html (Yahoo! News)]
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[2022 As-Suwayda clashes]]
***At least 17 people are killed and 40 others are injured in skirmishes between groups of pro-[[Bashar al-Assad|Assad]] and anti-[[government of Syria|government]] residents in [[As Suwayda]], [[Syria]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/7/28/at-least-17-dead-in-rare-clashes-in-syrias-sweida (Al Jazeera)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[2022 Russia–European Union gas dispute]]
**Authorities in [[Hanover]], [[Germany]], turn off heating and switch to cold showers in all public buildings, and also shut off public water fountains amid an [[2021–present global energy crisis|energy crisis]] after [[Gazprom]] reduced gas supplies to Germany through its [[Nord Stream]] pipeline. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-62335911 (BBC News)]
**Authorities in [[Berlin]] turn off lights at historic monuments and municipal buildings in the city in order to save electricity. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/jul/28/german-cities-impose-cold-showers-and-turn-off-fountains-in-face-of-russian-gas-crisis (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2021–2022 inflation surge]]
**The [[United States]] enters a [[recession|technical recession]] after its [[Economy of the United States|economy]] shrank for the 2nd consecutive quarter. [https://www.theguardian.com/business/2022/jul/28/us-economy-gdp-second-quarter (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/us-in-technical-recession-tgsjzk279 (''The Times'')]
*[[2020–present global chip shortage]]
**The [[United States Congress]] passes the Chips and Science Act of 2022 in order to boost semiconductor production in the United States and also boost competition with [[China]]. The bill will head to [[President of the United States|President]] [[Joe Biden]] for his signature. [https://www.cnbc.com/amp/2022/07/28/china-competitiveness-and-chip-bill-passes-house-goes-to-biden.html (CNBC)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[July 2022 United States floods]]
**[[Governor of Kentucky]] [[Andy Beshear]] declares a [[state of emergency]] for several counties in southeastern [[Kentucky]] due to historic floods, which have killed eight people. [https://www.lex18.com/news/covering-kentucky/gov-beshear-loss-of-life-expected-after-severe-flooding-in-kentucky-state-of-emergency-declared (WLEX-TV)]
*Flash flooding occurs on the [[Las Vegas Strip]] in [[Las Vegas]], [[Nevada]]. [https://www.reviewjournal.com/local/weather/downtown-las-vegas-sees-flooding-in-late-night-july-storm-2614211/amp/ (''Las Vegas Review-Journal'')]
*Four people are killed and nine others are injured by a [[landslide]] triggered by heavy rain in [[Tehran]], [[Iran]]. [https://apnews.com/article/floods-middle-east-iran-tehran-4ea1c9b02774de11fd5135b7161b4b9e (AP)]
*Fifteen people are killed and 47 others are injured after a bus crash in [[Esteli]], [[Nicaragua]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/least-13-venezuelans-killed-nicaraguan-traffic-accident-2022-07-28/ (Reuters)]
*Eight people are killed and four others are injured after a fire broke out in a hostel in [[Moscow]], [[Russia]]. [https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-fires-moscow-e46335eb534798e41cee886a08f9f9c7 (AP)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2022 monkeypox outbreak]]
**[[2022 monkeypox outbreak in the United States]]
***[[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] [[Chuck Schumer]] says that [[New York (state)|New York]] has received 110,000 doses of the monkeypox vaccine. [https://nypost.com/2022/07/28/new-york-finally-getting-110k-monkeypox-vaccine-doses-schumer/amp/ (''New York Post'')]
**Ahmed Ogwell, head of the [[Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention|Africa CDC]], reports that there are currently no [[Smallpox_vaccine#Third-generation|monkeypox or smallpox vaccines]] available in Africa to combat the ongoing [[monkeypox]] outbreak. [https://time.com/6201442/africa-monkeypox-vaccines/ (''Time'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Iran–Israel relations]]
**[[Law Enforcement Command of Islamic Republic of Iran|Iranian police]] arrest the alleged leader and four other members of a spy network suspected to be affiliated with [[Mossad]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/7/28/iran-arrests-suspected-israeli-linked-spies (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Lithuania–Russia relations]], [[Restriction of transit with the Kaliningrad Oblast]]
**Russia hands over a protest note to the [[Lithuanian Ministry of Foreign Affairs]] as [[Šiaulių bankas]], the only bank authorised to process payments for [[Kaliningrad Oblast|Kaliningrad]] rail transit, announced that it would phase out all payments in [[Russian ruble]]s in mid-August and ban all payments from Russia and Belarus, unless for [[humanitarian]] purposes or in order to fulfil international obligations, on 1 September. [https://www.lrt.lt/en/news-in-english/19/1748211/russian-envoy-hands-note-to-lithuania-over-kaliningrad-transit-payments (LRT)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Sentencing of Ben Oliver]]
**Cameras are allowed to film a criminal court case in [[England]] and [[Wales]] for the first time in history as a man, Ben Oliver, is sentenced to prison at [[London]]'s [[Old Bailey]] for [[manslaughter]] on live television. [https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/english-criminal-court-case-broadcast-tv-first-time-2022-07-28/ (Reuters)]

'''Science'''
*Researchers using [[AlphaFold]] have predicted the structures of 200 million [[protein]]s from 1 million species, covering nearly every known protein on the planet. [https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-022-02083-2 (''Nature'')]
